title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get—and in a Downtrend with 3.38% cash, paying 65.5x free cash flow is a luxury we cannot afford.
epigraph.author: Executive Investment Summary

web_blocks.html: Verdict: REJECTED (TIER_0, VALUATION) | Holding Action: NOT_HELD (0 shares) | Reference Close: $1,347.11 (2026-11-20) / $1,374.45 (2026-11-23 snapshot). Eli Lilly passes our fundamental business-quality screen (COMPOUNDER_PASS) on the strength of +53% Q3 2026 volume growth, 83.9% gross margins, and $18.98 billion in 9M 2026 free cash flow [33][34]. Yet a great business at the wrong price and wrong macro regime is still a pass.

At $1,347.11, LLY trades at 65.47x P/FCF (1.53% FCF yield vs. 5.04% U.S. 10-Year Treasury) and 27.00x forward P/E [36]. Our post-refresh underwriting incorporates 65.9% tirzepatide concentration, -15% consolidated net price erosion (-29% ex-U.S.), 2028 IRA Medicare selection of Trulicity and Verzenio (15.4% of FY25 sales), $18.24 billion in 9M BD/M&A cash outlays, $49.50 billion in gross debt, and $24.17 billion in accrued rebates [33][34]. That yields a 12-month Base Fair Value of $1,450.00 (+7.6%), a stressed Bear Case of $1,050.00 (-22.1%), and an Expected Value of $1,417.50 (+5.2%).

Against the snapshot invalidation stop of $1,172.53 (-13.0%), LLY offers 0.59:1 reward-to-risk at $1,347.11 and only 1.26:1 even on a pullback to $1,295.55 support—failing our 1.50:1 anti-hedging gate. With the U.S. market in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend (38.8% breadth > 50-day SMA) and consolidated portfolio cash at 3.38% ($2,540.35) versus a 22.0% floor, we reject both equity entry and the $9,317 February 2027 $1,360/$1,640 call spread (1,240.4 bps of NAV), allocating 100% of preserved capital to USD cash [35].

web_blocks.takeaway: LLY is a Tier-0 valuation rejection at $1,347.11: sub-1.50:1 support-zone asymmetry, -15% price erosion, and a 10-distribution-day Downtrend dictate holding 100% USD cash.

book_paragraphs: Eli Lilly is a scientific powerhouse priced for perfection in an unforgiving tape. Nine-month operating cash flow more than doubled to $27.42 billion in 2026, powered by Mounjaro and Zepbound, which now generate nearly two-thirds of company revenue. That operational dominance easily clears our fundamental quality bar.

Yet disciplined investing separates the quality of a business from the price of its stock. At the November 20, 2026 close of $1,347.11, Lilly trades at 65.5 times trailing free cash flow—a 1.53 percent cash yield while 10-year Treasuries yield 5.04 percent. Underneath the headline growth, consolidated net prices fell 15 percent year-over-year, Trulicity and Verzenio face 2028 Medicare price-setting, and nine-month M&A and IPR&D outlays reached $18.24 billion alongside $49.50 billion in gross debt.

Our re-underwriting places 12-month Base Fair Value at $1,450.00 per share, Bear Fair Value at $1,050.00, and probability-weighted Expected Value at $1,417.50. Against a $1,172.53 invalidation stop, neither the current price nor a pullback to $1,295.55 clears our 1.50-to-1 reward-to-risk minimum. In a ten-distribution-day Downtrend with portfolio cash at just 3.38 percent, we reject new equity and options exposure in Lilly and retain 100 percent of preserved capital in USD cash.
